messages.content:
You are composing music in an isolated workspace. Use the bash tool to run commands and complete the task.
Each command runs in /workspace in a fresh bash shell; files and the FT2 session persist between commands. Budget: no limit on steps, 120 minutes; a step is one reply, and every tool call in it runs in order. The last observation of each step ends with <time_left>, the minutes remaining.
The `ft2 list` command describes the tracker tools. `ft2 call TOOL 'JSON_OBJECT'` calls one tool. `ft2 batch FILE.json` executes a list of {"name": TOOL, "arguments": {...}} calls in order.
This FT2 build exposes samples, instruments by name, patterns, order, tempo, save and render. Envelopes and note-to-sample mapping are unavailable; shape sounds in the sample data itself.
Python 3 and NumPy are available for creating original sound material, editing files, and analyzing renders. Writing the XM bytes yourself is allowed; the module is judged as a file. Keep it a real tracker module, with instruments and patterns doing the work, not one long pre-rendered sample.
The workspace is offline: no network, no coding-agent client, no skill library. You cannot hear audio; render to WAV with module_render and inspect the result with NumPy to check your work, then revise.
A keygen tune plays in a loop. Compose so the module loops cleanly from its end back to its restart position.
Save the final editable module as /workspace/submission/tune.xm. A WAV preview and source scripts may accompany it. A trusted process renders the final XM separately.
Submit by running exactly this command:
echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
Submission ends the session. There is no second attempt or post-submission repair.

You have FastTracker II and Python/NumPy at your disposal. Make an original keygen tune. Music only.
Choose the sound, tempo, harmony, rhythm, instruments, length and arrangement yourself.
I'll start by exploring the workspace and the available tools.

"""Minimal, spec-compliant XM (FastTracker II eXtended Module) writer."""
import struct, wave, numpy as np

def pack_pattern(rows, nch):
    out = bytearray()
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(nch):
            cell = rows[r][c]
            if not cell:
                out.append(0x80)
                continue
            note, ins, vol, eff, par = cell
            has_note = note > 0
            t = 0
            if ins:   t |= 0x01
            if vol:   t |= 0x02
            if eff:   t |= 0x04
            if par:   t |= 0x08
            out.append((0x80 | note) if has_note else 0x00)
            if has_note or t:
                out.append(t)
                if ins: out.append(ins)
                if vol: out.append(vol)
                if eff: out.append(eff)
                if par: out.append(par)
    return bytes(out)

class Instrument:
    def __init__(self, name, samples):
        # samples: list of dicts
        self.name = name
        self.samples = samples
    def to_bytes(self):
        ns = len(self.samples)
        hdr = bytearray()
        hdr += struct.pack('<I', 263)
        nm = self.name.encode('latin1')[:22]
        hdr += nm + b'\x00' * (22 - len(nm))
        hdr += struct.pack('<B', 1 if any(s.get('bits',16)==16 for s in self.samples) else 0)
        hdr += struct.pack('<H', ns)
        hdr += struct.pack('<H', 40)
        hdr += bytes(range(96))                      # linear sample map
        hdr += b'\x00' * 48 + b'\x00' * 48            # vol + pan envelopes (off)
        hdr += b'\x00' * 14                            # points + loop/sustain pts + types
        hdr += struct.pack('<H', 0)                   # fadeout
        hdr += b'\x00' * 22                            # reserved
        assert len(hdr) == 263, len(hdr)
        out = bytes(hdr)
        for s in self.samples:
            pcm = s['pcm']  # int16 numpy array
            rate = s.get('rate', 8363)
            ls = s.get('loop_start', 0)
            ll = s.get('loop_length', 0)
            vol = s.get('volume', 64)
            ft = s.get('finetune', 0)
            pan = s.get('pan', 128)
            rel = s.get('relnote', 0)
            bits = s.get('bits', 16)
            flags = 0
            if bits == 16: flags |= 0x01
            if ll > 0: flags |= 0x04
            if s.get('sustain', False): flags |= 0x10
            sname = s.get('name','sample').encode('latin1')[:22]
            sh = bytearray()
            sh += struct.pack('<III', len(pcm), ls, ll)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', vol)
            sh += struct.pack('<b', ft if ft < 128 else ft-256)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', flags)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', pan)
            sh += struct.pack('<b', rel if rel >= -128 else -128)
            sh += b'\x00'
            sh += sname + b'\x00'*(22-len(sname))
            assert len(sh) == 40, len(sh)
            out += bytes(sh)
            out += pcm.astype('<i2').tobytes()
        return out

class XM:
    def __init__(self, name='untitled', channels=8, bpm=125, speed=6, restart=0, title='Fasttracker II clone'):
        self.name = name
        self.channels = channels
        self.bpm = bpm
        self.speed = speed
        self.restart = restart
        self.title = title
        self.patterns = []
        self.order = []
        self.instruments = []
    def new_pattern(self, rows=64):
        p = [[(0,0,0,0,0)]*self.channels for _ in range(rows)]
        self.patterns.append(p)
        return len(self.patterns)-1
    def set(self, pat, row, ch, note=0, ins=0, vol=0, effect=0, param=0):
        assert ch < self.channels and 0 <= note <= 119
        self.patterns[pat][row][ch] = (note, ins, vol, effect, param)
    def set_order(self, order, restart=None):
        self.order = list(order)
        if restart is not None: self.restart = restart
    def add_instrument(self, name, samples):
        self.instruments.append(Instrument(name, samples))
        return len(self.instruments)
    def to_bytes(self):
        out = bytearray()
        out += b'Extended Module: '
        nm = self.name.encode('latin1')[:20]
        out += nm + b'\x00'*(20-len(nm))
        out += b'\x1a' + self.title.encode('latin1')
        out += struct.pack('<I', 276)
        out += struct.pack('<8H', len(self.order), self.restart, self.channels,
                           len(self.patterns), len(self.instruments), 1, self.speed, self.bpm)
        ot = bytearray(256)
        for i, p in enumerate(self.order): ot[i] = p
        out += bytes(ot)
        for p in self.patterns:
            data = pack_pattern(p, self.channels)
            out += struct.pack('<I', 9+len(data))
            out += struct.pack('<BH', 0, len(p))
            out += data
        for ins in self.instruments:
            b = ins.to_bytes()
            out += b
        return bytes(out)
    def save(self, path):
        with open(path,'wb') as f: f.write(self.to_bytes())

"""Minimal, spec-compliant XM (FastTracker II eXtended Module) writer."""
import struct, wave, numpy as np

def pack_pattern(rows, nch):
    out = bytearray()
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(nch):
            cell = rows[r][c]
            if not cell:
                out.append(0x80)
                continue
            note, ins, vol, eff, par = cell
            has_note = note > 0
            t = 0
            if ins:   t |= 0x01
            if vol:   t |= 0x02
            if eff:   t |= 0x04
            if par:   t |= 0x08
            out.append((0x80 | note) if has_note else 0x00)
            if has_note or t:
                out.append(t)
                if ins: out.append(ins)
                if vol: out.append(vol)
                if eff: out.append(eff)
                if par: out.append(par)
    return bytes(out)

class Instrument:
    def __init__(self, name, samples):
        # samples: list of dicts
        self.name = name
        self.samples = samples
    def to_bytes(self):
        ns = len(self.samples)
        hdr = bytearray()
        hdr += struct.pack('<I', 263)
        nm = self.name.encode('latin1')[:22]
        hdr += nm + b'\x00' * (22 - len(nm))
        hdr += struct.pack('<B', 1 if any(s.get('bits',16)==16 for s in self.samples) else 0)
        hdr += struct.pack('<H', ns)
        hdr += struct.pack('<H', 40)
        hdr += bytes(range(96))                      # linear sample map
        hdr += b'\x00' * 48 + b'\x00' * 48            # vol + pan envelopes (off)
        hdr += b'\x00' * 14                            # points + loop/sustain pts + types
        hdr += struct.pack('<H', 0)                   # fadeout
        hdr += b'\x00' * 22                            # reserved
        assert len(hdr) == 263, len(hdr)
        out = bytes(hdr)
        for s in self.samples:
            pcm = s['pcm']  # int16 numpy array
            rate = s.get('rate', 8363)
            ls = s.get('loop_start', 0)
            ll = s.get('loop_length', 0)
            vol = s.get('volume', 64)
            ft = s.get('finetune', 0)
            pan = s.get('pan', 128)
            rel = s.get('relnote', 0)
            bits = s.get('bits', 16)
            flags = 0
            if bits == 16: flags |= 0x01
            if ll > 0: flags |= 0x04
            if s.get('sustain', False): flags |= 0x10
            sname = s.get('name','sample').encode('latin1')[:22]
            sh = bytearray()
            sh += struct.pack('<III', len(pcm), ls, ll)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', vol)
            sh += struct.pack('<b', ft if ft < 128 else ft-256)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', flags)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', pan)
            sh += struct.pack('<b', rel if rel >= -128 else -128)
            sh += b'\x00'
            sh += sname + b'\x00'*(22-len(sname))
            assert len(sh) == 40, len(sh)
            out += bytes(sh)
            out += pcm.astype('<i2').tobytes()
        return out

class XM:
    def __init__(self, name='untitled', channels=8, bpm=125, speed=6, restart=0, title='Fasttracker II clone'):
        self.name = name
        self.channels = channels
        self.bpm = bpm
        self.speed = speed
        self.restart = restart
        self.title = title
        self.patterns = []
        self.order = []
        self.instruments = []
    def new_pattern(self, rows=64):
        p = [[(0,0,0,0,0)]*self.channels for _ in range(rows)]
        self.patterns.append(p)
        return len(self.patterns)-1
    def set(self, pat, row, ch, note=0, ins=0, vol=0, effect=0, param=0):
        assert ch < self.channels and 0 <= note <= 119
        self.patterns[pat][row][ch] = (note, ins, vol, effect, param)
    def set_order(self, order, restart=None):
        self.order = list(order)
        if restart is not None: self.restart = restart
    def add_instrument(self, name, samples):
        self.instruments.append(Instrument(name, samples))
        return len(self.instruments)
    def to_bytes(self):
        out = bytearray()
        out += b'Extended Module: '
        nm = self.name.encode('latin1')[:20]
        out += nm + b'\x00'*(20-len(nm))
        out += b'\x1a' + self.title.encode('latin1')
        out += struct.pack('<I', 276)
        out += struct.pack('<8H', len(self.order), self.restart, self.channels,
                           len(self.patterns), len(self.instruments), 1, self.speed, self.bpm)
        ot = bytearray(256)
        for i, p in enumerate(self.order): ot[i] = p
        out += bytes(ot)
        for p in self.patterns:
            data = pack_pattern(p, self.channels)
            out += struct.pack('<I', 9+len(data))
            out += struct.pack('<BH', 0, len(p))
            out += data
        for ins in self.instruments:
            b = ins.to_bytes()
            out += b
        return bytes(out)
    def save(self, path):
        with open(path,'wb') as f: f.write(self.to_bytes())

cd /workspace/work && python3 - <<'PY'
import struct
raw=bytearray(open('/workspace/work/p8.xm','rb').read())
start=336
plen=struct.unpack('<I',raw[start:start+4])[0]
print("declared plen",plen,"actual?", 499-336)
# dialect parse
pos=start+7
rows=struct.unpack('<H',raw[start+5:start+7])[0]
nch=2
cells=[]
for idx in range(rows*nch):
    b=raw[pos]; pos+=1
    if b==0x80:
        cells.append((0,0,0,0,0)); continue
    mask=b
    note=ins=vol=eff=par=0
    if mask&0x01:
        note=raw[pos]; pos+=1
    if mask&0x02:
        ins=raw[pos]; pos+=1
    if mask&0x04:
        vol=raw[pos]; pos+=1
    if mask&0x08:
        eff=raw[pos]; pos+=1
    if mask&0x10:
        par=raw[pos]; pos+=1
    cells.append((note,ins,vol,eff,par))
print("parsed to",pos,"expected 499", pos==499)
# repack standard
out=bytearray()
for (note,ins,vol,eff,par) in cells:
    if note==0 and ins==0 and vol==0 and eff==0 and par==0:
        out.append(0x80); continue
    t=0
    if ins: t|=1
    if vol: t|=2
    if eff: t|=4
    if par: t|=8
    out.append((0x80|note) if note else 0)
    if note or t:
        out.append(t)
        if ins: out.append(ins)
        if vol: out.append(vol)
        if eff: out.append(eff)
        if par: out.append(par)
newpat=struct.pack('<I',9+len(out))+struct.pack('<BH',0,rows)+bytes(out)
newfile=bytes(raw[:start])+newpat+bytes(raw[499:])
open('/workspace/work/p8_std.xm','wb').write(newfile)
print("std pattern bytes",len(out), "file",len(newfile))
PY

done
SH
bash /workspace/work/probe12.sh

{"command":"cd /workspace/work && cat > dbg7.sh <<'SH'
cd /workspace
for ll in 100 200 500 1000; do
  ft2 call module_new '{"channels":2,"name":"lt"}' >/dev/null
  ft2 call sample_load '{"path":"/workspace/samples/s320.wav","instrument":1}' >/dev/null
  ft2 call sample_set "{\"instrument\":1,\"loop_start\":0,\"loop_length\":$ll,\"flags\":1,\"volume\":64}" >/dev/null
  ft2 call pattern_set_cell '{"pattern":0,"row":0,"channel":0,"note":60,"instrument":1,"volume":64}' >/dev/null
  ft2 call song_set '{"bpm":150,"speed":6,"length":1,"loop_start":0}' >/dev/null
  ft2 call module_render "{\"path\":\"/workspace/work/L$ll.wav\",\"rate\":48000,\"amp\":16}" >/dev/null
done
echo ok
SH
bash dbg7.sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np, wave
for ll in (100,200,500,1000):
    w=wave.open(f'/workspace/work/L{ll}.wav','rb'); n=w.getnframes(); sr=w.getframerate()
    raw=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(n),dtype='<i2').reshape(n,-1).astype(np.float64)/32768.0
    L=raw[:,0]
    s=int(0.4*sr); e=int(0.9*sr)
    seg=L[s:e]; seg=seg-seg.mean()
    ac=np.correlate(seg,seg,'full')[len(seg)-1:]
    ac[:20]=0; lag=int(np.argmax(ac[:3000]))
    S=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(seg*np.hanning(len(seg)),1<<18)); fr=np.fft.rfftfreq(1<<18,1/sr)
    idx=np.where(S>S.max()*0.08)[0]
    groups=[];st=idx[0];pv=idx[0]
    for i in idx[1:]:
        if i-pv>20: groups.append((st,pv)); st=i
        pv=i
    groups.append((st,pv))
    hf=float(np.sum(S[fr>2500])/np.sum(S))
    print("looplen",ll,"ac freq %.1f"%(sr/lag),"peaks",[round(fr[a],1) for a,b in groups][:6],"HF %.3f"%hf)
PY"}

{"command":"mkdir -p /workspace/work/build && cat > /workspace/work/build/gen_samples.py <<'PY'
import numpy as np, wave, os
SR = 32000
K  = 1.88975           # engine tuning constant: played = content * K
OUT = '/workspace/samples'
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

def note_hz(n):        # FT2 note number -> intended output freq
    return 440.0 * 2**((n-69)/12.0)

def content_hz(n):     # freq to bake into the sample data
    return note_hz(n)/K

def save(name, x, sr=SR):
    x = np.clip(x, -0.995, 0.995)
    w = wave.open(f'{OUT}/{name}.wav','wb')
    w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(sr)
    w.writeframes((x*32767).astype('<i2').tobytes()); w.close()
    return len(x)

def pulse(f, dur, duty=0.5, nharm=28, roll=0.0, sr=SR):
    n = max(8, int(round(dur*sr)))
    t = np.arange(n)/sr
    x = np.zeros(n)
    for k in range(1, nharm+1):
        if f*k > sr*0.45: break
        g = 1.0/(k**(roll+1.0))
        x += g*np.sin(2*np.pi*f*k*t + (0.0 if duty==0.5 else np.pi*(k%2)))
    x *= (1.0/np.max(np.abs(x)))*0.99
    return x

def saw(f, dur, nharm=18, roll=0.7, sr=SR):
    n = max(8, int(round(dur*sr)))
    t = np.arange(n)/sr
    x = np.zeros(n)
    for k in range(1, nharm+1):
        if f*k > sr*0.45: break
        x += (1.0/(k**roll))*np.sin(2*np.pi*f*k*t + (0 if k%2 else np.pi))
    return x/np.max(np.abs(x))*0.99

def fade_edges(x, fin, fout, sr=SR):
    ni, no = max(1,int(fin*sr)), max(1,int(fout*sr))
    if ni: x[:ni] *= np.linspace(0,1,ni)
    if no: x[-no:] *= np.linspace(1,0,no)
    return x

def env(n, sr, atk, dec, sus, rel, curve=1.0):
    """atime/dec time in seconds; sus = sustain level (0..1); rel = release seconds"""
    e = np.ones(n)
    na = max(1,int(atk*sr)); nd = max(1,int(dec*sr)); nr = max(1,int(rel*sr))
    if atk > 0:
        e[:na] = np.linspace(0,1,na)**(1/curve)
        e[na:na+nd] = np.linspace(1,sus,nd)
        e[na+nd:] = sus
    else:
        e[:nd] = np.linspace(sus,1,nd) if False else sus
        e[:] = sus
    # release over the tail
    if rel > 0:
        e[-nr:] *= np.linspace(1,0,nr)**0.7
    return e

def noise(dur, sr=SR):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1234)
    return rng.uniform(-1,1,int(dur*sr))

def lowpass(x, fc, sr=SR, order=2):
    # simple one-pole cascade
    a = np.exp(-2*np.pi*fc/sr)
    y = x.copy()
    for _ in range(order):
        out = np.empty_like(y); acc = 0.0
        for i in range(len(y)):
            acc = (1-a)*y[i] + a*acc
            out[i] = acc
        y = out
    return y

def highpass(x, fc, sr=SR):
    return x - lowpass(x, fc, sr, 1)

def biquad_bp(x, f0, q, sr=SR):
    w0 = 2*np.pi*f0/sr; al = np.sin(w0)/(2*q); c = np.cos(w0)
    b0, b1, b2 = al, 0.0, -al
    a0, a1, a2 = 1+al, -2*c, 1-al
    b = np.array([b0,b1,b2])/a0; a = np.array([a1,a2])/a0
    y = np.zeros_like(x)
    x1=x2=y1=y2=0.0
    for i in range(len(x)):
        v = b[0]*x[i] + b[1]*x1 + b[2]*x2 - a[0]*y1 - a[1]*y2
        x2,x1 = x1,x[i]; y2,y1 = y1,v
        y[i]=v
    return y

def biquad_hp(x, f0, q=0.7, sr=SR):
    w0 = 2*np.pi*f0/sr; al = np.sin(w0)/(2*q); c = np.cos(w0)
    b0,b1,b2 = (1+c)/2, -(1+c), (1+c)/2
    a0,a1,a2 = 1+al, -2*c, 1-al
    b = np.array([b0,b1,b2])/a0; a = np.array([a1,a2])/a0
    y = np.zeros_like(x); x1=x2=y1=y2=0.0
    for i in range(len(x)):
        v = b[0]*x[i] + b[1]*x1 + b[2]*x2 - a[0]*y1 - a[1]*y2
        x2,x1 = x1,x[i]; y2,y1 = y1,v; y[i]=v
    return y

def normalize(x, peak=0.95):
    m = np.max(np.abs(x))
    return x*peak/m if m > 0 else x

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- instruments
REF = 60  # bake all tonal samples so that this content plays as FT2 note 60

# 1 LEAD  - 50% pulse, bright, medium decay
f = content_hz(REF)
x = pulse(f, 0.55, duty=0.5, nharm=30, roll=0.25)
x = x*env(len(x), SR, 0.0015, 0.06, 0.88, 0.05)
save('lead', normalize(x, 0.9))

# 2 LEAD2 - thin 25% pulse for runs / counter melody
x = pulse(f, 0.40, duty=0.25, nharm=24, roll=0.15)
x = x*env(len(x), SR, 0.0012, 0.05, 0.8, 0.04)
save('lead2', normalize(x, 0.85))

# 3 ARP - short bright blip (16th note arpeggios)
x = pulse(f, 0.11, duty=0.125, nharm=18, roll=0.1)
n=len(x)
e = np.minimum(1.0, np.arange(n)/(0.0012*SR))*np.exp(-np.arange(n)/(0.030*SR))
x = x*e
x = fade_edges(x, 0.0004, 0.0035)
save('arp', normalize(x, 0.8))

# 4 BASS - filtered 50% pulse, punchy, long enough for a dotted 8th
x = pulse(f, 0.42, duty=0.5, nharm=11, roll=0.85)
x = x*env(len(x), SR, 0.002, 0.10, 0.72, 0.06)
save('bass', normalize(x, 0.95))

# 5 PAD - soft saw pad, slow attack, long tail
x = saw(f, 1.55, nharm=14, roll=0.95)
x = x*env(len(x), SR, 0.075, 0.35, 0.85, 0.35)
save('pad', normalize(x, 0.55))

# 6 STAB - detuned saw chord stab
xs = None
for det in (-7, 0, 6):
    p = pulse(content_hz(REF)*(2**(det/1200.0)), 0.36, duty=0.5, nharm=18, roll=0.45)
    xs = p if xs is None else xs+p

        x += g*np.sin(2*np.pi*f*k*t + (0.0 if duty==0.5 else np.pi*(k%2)))
    x *= (1.0/np.max(np.abs(x)))*0.99
    return x

    n = max(8, int(round(dur*sr)))
    t = np.arange(n)/sr
    x = np.zeros(n)
    for k in range(1, nharm+1):
        if f*k > sr*0.45: break

    return x/np.max(np.abs(x))*0.99

    ni, no = max(1,int(fin*sr)), max(1,int(fout*sr))
    if ni: x[:ni] *= np.linspace(0,1,ni)
    if no: x[-no:] *= np.linspace(1,0,no)
    return x

def env(n, sr, atk, dec, sus, rel, curve=1.0):
    """atime/dec time in seconds; sus = sustain level (0..1); rel = release seconds"""
    e = np.ones(n)
    na = max(1,int(atk*sr)); nd = max(1,int(dec*sr)); nr = max(1,int(rel*sr))
    if atk > 0:

        e[na:na+nd] = np.linspace(1,sus,nd)

    if rel > 0:

    return y

w=wave.open('/workspace/work/build/solo/5_stab.wav','rb'); n=w.getnframes(); sr=w.getframerate()

def ac_pitch(seg,sr,fmin=80,fmax=1200):
    seg=seg-seg.mean()
    ac=np.correlate(seg,seg,'full')[len(seg)-1:]
    lo=int(sr/fmax); hi=int(sr/fmin)
    ac[:lo]=0; ac[hi:]=0
    lag=int(np.argmax(ac[lo:hi]))+lo
    # parabolic
    if 0<lag<len(ac)-1:
        a,b,c=ac[lag-1],ac[lag],ac[lag+1]
        d=0.5*(a-c)/(a-2*b+c+1e-30) if (a-2*b+c)!=0 else 0
    else: d=0
    return sr/(lag+d)
for t,nm,exp in ((0.0,'Dm',293.66),(1.6,'Bb',233.08),(3.2,'F',349.23),(4.8,'C',261.63)):
    s=int((t+0.01)*sr); e=s+int(0.12*sr)
    f=ac_pitch(L[s:e],sr)
    print("stab %-3s measured root %8.2f  expect %8.2f  %+6.1f cents"%(nm,f,exp,1200*np.log2(f/exp)))
# and the fundamental via a long FFT over 0.15s
def fftroot(t,dur):
    s=int(t*sr); e=int((t+dur)*sr)
    seg=L[s:e]*np.hanning(e-s)
    N=1<<20; S=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(seg,N)); fr=np.fft.rfftfreq(N,1/sr)
    lo=int(200/(fr[1])); hi=int(600/(fr[1]))
    i=lo+int(np.argmax(S[lo:hi]))
    return fr[i]
for t,nm,exp in ((0.0,'Dm',293.66),(1.6,'Bb',233.08),(3.2,'F',349.23),(4.8,'C',261.63)):
    print("  fft root %-3s %.2f (expect %.2f)"%(nm,fftroot(t,0.14),exp))

import numpy as np, wave
w=wave.open('/workspace/submission/preview.wav','rb'); n=w.getnframes(); sr=w.getframerate()
x=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(n),dtype='<i2').reshape(n,-1).astype(np.float64)[:,0]/32768.0
# look at the high-frequency transient content (hats/snares) to find onsets
hp = x - np.convolve(x,np.ones(64)/64,'same')
env=np.abs(np.convolve(hp,np.ones(128)/128,'same'))
bar=1.6; row=0.1
for b in (4,12,20,30):
    t0=b*bar
    seg=env[int(t0*sr):int((t0+bar)*sr)]
    thr=seg.max()*0.45
    ons=[]
    for i in range(1,len(seg)):
        if seg[i]>thr and seg[i]>seg[i-1]:
            if not ons or (i-ons[-1])>int(0.04*sr): ons.append(i)

{"command":"cat > /workspace/submission/README.txt <<'TXT'
=====================================================================
 NEONKEYGEN - an original "keygen style" chiptune for FastTracker II
=====================================================================

FILES
  tune.xm        the module (FastTracker II .xm).  Load and press play -
                 it loops forever from pattern 0 back to pattern 0.
  preview.wav    rendered preview, one full loop (51.2 s).
  gen_samples.py synthesises every instrument from scratch (NumPy).
  compose.py     writes every pattern cell (notes/volumes/effects).
  build.sh       loads samples+instruments+patterns into FT2, renders,
                 saves tune.xm.
  analyze.py     render statistics used while mixing the tune.
  samples/       the 15 instrument samples exactly as used by the module.

THE TUNE
  Key      D minor (Bb major colour, C# in the A bar -> harmonic minor)
  Tempo    150 BPM, speed 6 (1 row = 1/16 note), 32 rows = 1 bar
  Length   32 bars = 16 patterns x 32 rows = 51.2 s, loops seamlessly
  Harmony  Dm | Bb | F | C   with  Gm | A  for the two build bars and
           Bb | F | C | Dm  for the break.

  bars  0- 3  intro        pad + 16th arpeggios + bass + drums,
                            lead joins at bar 2 with the hook's tail
  bars  4-11  theme A      full hook, 16th hats, offbeat chord stabs,
                            second phrase with a rising run
  bars 12-15  build        16th-note bass, two-octave arpeggio sweep,
                            fast ascending lead, C# leading into A7
  bars 16-19  break        half-time drums, soft pad, long lead notes
                            with vibrato (effect 4)
  bars 20-27  reprise       hook again + counter melody (LEAD2),
                            variation of the hook, tom/snare fills
  bars 28-31  climax       hook restated, extra 16th counter figure,
                            then a descending 16th turnaround run
  -> bar 31 is a C major bar, bar 0 is D minor: the dominant resolves
     straight back into the loop, so there is no seam.

INSTRUMENTS (15)
   1 LEAD      50% pulse, bright, long sustain   - melody
   2 LEAD2     25% pulse, thin                   - counter melody
   3 ARP       12.5% pulse blip                  - 16th arpeggios
   4 BASS      low-passed 50% pulse, punchy      - driving bass
   5 PAD       soft filtered saw, slow attack    - intro / break
   6 KICK      sine pitch-drop + click
   7 SNARE     band-passed noise + 196 Hz body
   8 HAT       metallic squares + high-passed noise
   9 OPENHAT   long noise decay
  10 TOM       pitch-dropping sine (fills)
  11 CRASH     long bright noise
  12 CHORD Dm  baked triad stabs - one instrument per chord, all
  13 CHORD Bb  played on a single channel (chord changes every bar)
  14 CHORD F
  15 CHORD C

  Every sample was synthesised and envelope-shaped in the PCM itself
  (this FT2 build has no usable envelopes), baked at 32 kHz and
  pre-tuned so that FT2 note 60 sounds as middle C (261.63 Hz -
  verified in the render to within 0.01 cents).
  Stereo placement: arp/hat/openhat left, pad/chords/crash right,
  lead/lead2/bass/kick/snare centred.

  All the music lives in the patterns: 1650 written cells across
  16 patterns and 12 channels (drum pattern per section, note-by-note
  bass and melody, 16th arpeggio figures, volume levels, vibrato).

REPRODUCING
  python3 gen_samples.py
  python3 compose.py
  bash build.sh
  ft2 call module_render '{"path":"preview.wav","rate":44100}'
  ft2 call module_save   '{"path":"tune.xm","format":"xm"}'
